Side A · Recipe 04

Backwards dream

Reverse echoes, slow melody

A slow melody whose echoes play in reverse, swelling into each note before it arrives, inside a reverb that builds slowly. Like a tape played backwards in a dream.

Level
Easy
Setup
10 min
Key
D minor
  1. What you'll hear
  2. 1. PERfourMER: a soft, clear note
  3. 2. Grand Canyon: everything backwards
  4. 3. NightSky: a slow-building wash
  5. 4. The OXI One: play it

What you'll hear

Each note you play comes back reversed: it swells up instead of fading out. The reverb builds slowly too, so the whole thing breathes in rather than out.

The trick: the Grand Canyon's REVERSE listens for each new note and reverses what follows it. A light on the pedal blinks each time it hears one, so you can tune it by eye.

1. PERfourMER: a soft, clear note

Synth channel 1 on MIDI channel 1; channels 3 and 4 VOLUME down.

  • 1WAVEsinetrianglesquaresawnoiseEXTSoft, clear notes reverse cleanly.
  • 2OCTAVE8'Middle register.
  • 3CUTOFFnoonHalf open.
  • 4RESONANCEminClean.
  • 5ATTACKminA clear start, so the pedal can hear each note.
  • 6DECAY11 o'clockMedium.
  • 7SUSTAIN10 o'clockA little held.
  • 8RELEASE11 o'clockMedium fade.
  • 9PANnoonIn the main left output, which feeds the pedals.

2. Grand Canyon: everything backwards

  • 1DELAY TYPEREVERSEReverse echoes, with a detector that listens for each new note.
  • 2SENSITIVITY (left mini knob)noonThen adjust: the REVERSE LED should blink on every note the OXI plays, and not in between.
  • 3MOD DEPTH (right mini knob)10 o'clockA little movement in the reversed sound.
  • 4DELAY1 o'clockLong: the reversed swell needs time.
  • 5FEEDBACK10 o'clockOne or two repeats.
  • 6DELAY LVL2 o'clockUp to where dry and reverse are both full: past 2 o'clock the dry note starts to drop.
  • TempoDon't tap: set it with the DELAY knob aboveA long, free delay suits the slow melody better than a locked one.

3. NightSky: a slow-building wash

  • 1TEXTUREsparsedensediffuseSlow-building: excels at swell and reverse-like textures.
  • 2LENGTH1 o'clockMedium-long.
  • 3SIZE/PITCHnoonMiddle.
  • 4FILTERregenlow passDarkens as it decays.
  • 5HIGH CUTnoonSoft.
  • 6LOW CUT10 o'clockRoom for the bass.
  • 7TARGETverbpitchfilterModulation moves the HIGH CUT: the brightness drifts.
  • 8SHAPEtrianglesquarerampsawrandomenvEven.
  • 9SPEED8 o'clockVery slow.
  • 10DEPTH11 o'clockNoticeable drift.
  • 11SHIMMER (knob)minOff.
  • 12GLIMMERhighlowoffMysterious lows.
  • 13DRYnoonUnity.
  • 14REVERBnoonEven with the dry signal.

4. The OXI One: play it

  1. Tempo 60–75 BPM: slow is the point.
  2. Sequencer 1 (Mono, Ch 1): a slow melody in D minor (try D, F, A, C, E), one note every 4 steps, with rests. Each note about 2 steps long (hold the pad, turn knob 3).
  3. Sequencer 2 (Mono, Ch 2, the bass patch from the rig page): a low D, one long note per two bars, tied.

You got it right when

  • The REVERSE LED blinks once per note.
  • Each note is followed by a swell that rises into silence instead of fading.

5. The performance

  • Turn SENSITIVITY down while it plays: the pedal hears fewer notes, and the reversed phrases get longer and stranger.
  • Press INFINITE on the NightSky over a reversed swell to hold it as a pad.

If it sounds wrong

  • No reverse, or random chops: watch the REVERSE LED. If it doesn't blink on each note, turn SENSITIVITY up; if it blinks between notes, turn it down.
  • Reverse sounds too quiet: DELAY LVL up, but stay at or below 2 o'clock to keep the dry note.

Sources

  • Grand Canyon manual: REVERSE, SENSITIVITY and the blinking LED (p. 17), DELAY LVL (p. 8).
  • NightSky manual: diffuse "swell, and even reverse-like textures" (p. 5), TARGET filter (p. 10).
  • PERfourMER MKII manual: envelope (p. 20).
  • OXI One MKII manual: steps and gates (pp. 51, 55).
